title: A number in range
description: Write `int readIntInRange(int low, int high)`. It keeps reading until it gets a whole number between `low` and `high` (both allowed). Text that is not a number, and numbers outside the range, are both rejected.
hints: Use an endless loop, `while (true)`, and `return` from inside it as soon as you have a good number.

When `std::cin >> value` fails (the user typed letters), `std::cin` is in a failed state: call `std::cin.clear()` and then `std::cin.ignore(std::numeric_limits<std::streamsize>::max(), '\n')` to throw the bad line away before trying again.
unitTests:
TEST("accepts a value in range") { int v{}; xenon::run_with_input("5
", [&] { v = readIntInRange(1, 10); }); CHECK_EQ(v, 5); }
TEST("rejects numbers outside the range") { int v{}; xenon::run_with_input("0
11
99
10
", [&] { v = readIntInRange(1, 10); }); CHECK_EQ(v, 10); }
TEST("rejects text and numbers together") { int v{}; xenon::run_with_input("abc
500
q
3
", [&] { v = readIntInRange(1, 6); }); CHECK_EQ(v, 3); }
